CAR.head: A big edge for the Hurricanes
CAR.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. If the Jets want to spoil it, start with getting good looks.

WPG.head: The Hurricanes should be favored
WPG.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. To pull this off, the Jets can start with getting good looks, plus Stuart Skinner stealing the show.

story.head: The Jets need a win
paras: The Jets are winless in eight (0-6-2), while Carolina has won three straight. The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Winnipeg on Oct 17. Going in, the Jets are seventh in the Central (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Canes are first in the NHL.

The Jets have played better than their record (.393) says: their chances are worth about .451, and their finishing has held them back. The Hurricanes’ record (.800) is about what their chances are worth.

The Hurricanes (1st) and the Jets (2nd) both create chances on the penalty kill. The Jets rarely ice the puck (5th), but take a lot of low-quality shots (30th). Winnipeg has scored 2.43 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. On the other side, the Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). Carolina has scored 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league, and allowed 2.33, the third fewest. The Hurricanes are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Jets, and the Hurricanes’ forecheck could keep the Jets pinned in their own end.

Kyle Connor (11 G / 4 A / 15 P in 14 GP) leads the Jets in scoring, and Mark Scheifele (2 G / 10 A / 12 P in 14 GP) is next in line. Sebastian Aho (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 15 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, and Logan Stankoven (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL.
Stuart Skinner (3-3-3 / .899 SV% in 9 GS) is in line to start for Winnipeg. Pyotr Kochetkov (9-0-0 / .918 SV% in 9 GS) has been a rock in net for Carolina and will likely start.

At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to send Martinook, Jankowski and Jarvis out against opponents’ second lines, so watch for them against Connor, Björck and Mercer. One more thing: the Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.
